paper_title: First Results from the Taiwan Axion Search Experiment with Haloscope at 19.6 $μ$eV
coupling_convention: |g_agammagamma| in GeV^-1 (plotted axis in units of 10^-14 GeV^-1, multiplier applied)
notes: TASEH first results (CD102 run, Oct-Nov 2021), haloscope search covering 4.70750-4.79815 GHz (19.4687-19.8436 ueV). No axion candidates found; 95% C.L. upper limits on |g_agamma| range from 5.3e-14 to 8.9e-14 GeV^-1 with an average of 8.2e-14 GeV^-1 (a factor of 11 above KSVZ). The emitted points use the paper's average limit spanning the stated mass range since the full frequency-resolved limit data is only in Fig. 2, not tabulated. Assumes axions constitute 100% of local DM with rho = 0.45 GeV/cm^3, standard Maxwellian line shape with <v^2>=(270 km/s)^2. Two narrow frequency ranges (4.71017-4.71019 GHz and 4.74730-4.74738 GHz) are excluded from the limits due to identified non-axion interference signals. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 49)) | Vision: TASEH first results, 95% C.L. limit on |g_agammagamma| over 4.70750-4.79815 GHz (m_a = 19.4687-19.8436 ueV).
